task_brief: This is day 3 of "Stories in Motion: Drama and Movement". That is unit 4 in grade 3. Today is a guided practice (first pass) about telling a story with expression. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Create and share, privately or with a small audience, a short original movement story or scene. Today helps by working on telling a story with expression. Your unit also covers character and imagination, simple movement vocabulary, telling a story with expression, and space and levels in movement. Today adds real evidence toward your unit project.
primary_task: Make two small studies about telling a story with expression. You may look at the example while you work. After each one, write the choice you made. Write what you wanted it to do. Keep both studies even if you do not like them. They show your process. Then circle the one move you could not do without the example. You will test that next time. This work stays private unless you want to share it. Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about telling a story with expression. It is part of "Stories in Motion: Drama and Movement". Later days in this unit cover other things, like character and imagination. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about telling a story with expression; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 3 you need one clear try with a grown-up nearby. Say or write your reason in a sentence or two. Drawings, objects, or spoken answers are all fine.

ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g3-arts-music-u04-l03

Lesson focus: telling a story with expression

Resource type: ACADEMY_CREATED_SCAFFOLD

GUIDED SCAFFOLD A — Build two four-beat scene or movement studies. Fill 1 WHERE/START; 2 WANT; 3 OBSTACLE OR CHANGE; 4 CHOICE/END. Add one pause and one change of distance. In Study 2 change either pause or distance, not both. Name the intended effect and exact beat creating it. Paper figures, arrows, or writing count fully. Use it to study telling a story with expression; describe evidence before judging and adapt the example rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task.

critique_criteria: You made two studies with the example nearby and kept both.
Each one says the choice you made and what you wanted it to do.
You circled one move you could not do without the example.
Your work stayed private, seen only by you and maybe one trusted grown-up.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting telling a story with expression.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for telling a story with expression follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for telling a story with expression, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for telling a story with expression works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of telling a story with expression, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking telling a story with expression mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply telling a story with expression under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on telling a story with expression rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
